e.etymology: An American variant of Alonzo, a Spanish form of Alfonso, from a Visigothic name usually analyzed as adal (noble) and funs (ready).

e.meaning: horse protection; later read as rose of the world
e.etymology: A variant of Rosamund, from Germanic words for horse and protection. Medieval readers reinterpreted it as Latin rosa munda, pure rose, or rosa mundi, rose of the world.
An American name of the 1960s that adds the De- prefix to Lisa, a short form of Elizabeth. Delisa is also an Italian surname.
Originally Chas., the written abbreviation of Charles, which old records show as if it were the name; now also a nickname said like Chaz. Charles comes from a Germanic word for a free man.
Either a 20th-century spelling of Trudy or the German pet form Trudi. Both shorten Gertrude, from the Germanic elements for spear and strength.
A spelling of Christie, the pet form of Christine and Christina, from Latin Christiana, a Christian woman. In Romania Cristi is a man's name, short for Cristian.
A spelling of Rob, the short form of Robert, also a surname from the same medieval pet form. Robert joins the Germanic elements hrod (fame) and beraht (bright).

assoc.t: Robb Stark, the Young Wolf in Game of Thrones

e.etymology: A spelling of Murray, the Scottish surname from the region of Moray, an old Celtic name meaning settlement by the sea.
A phonetic American spelling of Elise, the French and German short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.
A spelling of Barry, the English form of Irish Barra, a short form of Fionnbarr, fair-headed, and also of Bearach, sharp. Barrie is a Scottish surname too, as in the Peter Pan author J. M. Barrie.
The name of the enchantress in Torquato Tasso's 1581 epic Jerusalem Delivered, who became the heroine of operas by Lully, Haydn, Rossini and Dvorak. It is first known from Tasso's poem.
A spelling of Carissa, a form of Charissa, which Edmund Spenser built on Greek charis, grace, for The Faerie Queene. It is often also read as Latin carissima, dearest.
A respelling of Candace. Kandake was the title of the queens of ancient Kush, in what is now Sudan, and appears in the Book of Acts as if it were a personal name.
A surname spelling of Randall, the medieval English everyday form of Randolph, from Germanic words for shield rim and wolf.
A surname used as a first name. As a Swedish surname Lindell is built on lind, the linden tree; an English surname of the same form comes from a place name.
The French, German and Scandinavian short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. English speakers often treat it as a variant of Lisa.
namesakes: Lise Meitner (physicist who helped discover nuclear fission)

e.etymology: A respelling of Kristen and Kristin, Scandinavian forms of Christina, from Latin Christiana, a Christian woman.
An African-American name of the 1980s that puts the La- prefix on Toria, a short form of Victoria, Latin for victory.
Built on Jon or John with the -ell ending. In the 1930s it was mostly a girls' name, in the manner of Jo plus Nell; recent American use is for boys.
A Scottish surname from Raeburn in the Borders, a place name made of Scots rae (roebuck) and burn (stream).
A clipped spelling of Reginald, the Latinized form of Reynold, from Germanic ragin (counsel) and wald (rule).
An American variant of Naomi, from Hebrew Naomi, pleasantness. In the Bible Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth.
An older spelling of Betsy, a pet form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.

assoc.t: Betsey Johnson, fashion and accessories label

e.etymology: The German form of Ernest, originally a byname from Old High German ernust, seriousness or vigor, and a medieval ducal name in Germany.
An elaboration of Cheryl with the -lyn ending. It is the birth name of the singer Cher, born Cherilyn Sarkisian in 1946.
Matches Spanish loma, hill, familiar from Western place names such as Loma Linda and Point Loma. Why it was taken up as a girls' name around 1900 is not recorded.
In Italy Loris is a men's name, and in Greece it is a short form of Lykourgos. How the American name of the early 1900s arose is not recorded.
e.note: A loris is also a small, slow-moving nocturnal primate of South and Southeast Asia.

e.etymology: A short form of Nathaniel and Nathan, from Hebrew roots meaning God has given and he gave. It is also used for Natalie and Natasha.
namesakes: Nat King Cole (singer and jazz pianist)
Nat Turner (leader of the 1831 slave rebellion)
e.note: Sounds the same as gnat, the tiny biting insect.

e.etymology: As an American first name of the 1970s and 1980s, a clipped form in the family of Dwayne and Antwan, said like Dwon. Dwan is also an Irish surname.
A short form of Florence and Flora. Florence comes from Latin florens, flowering or flourishing; Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers.

assoc.t: Aunt Flo, a euphemism for a menstrual period
Flo, period and pregnancy tracking app

e.note: Aunt Flo is a common euphemism for a period, and flow is an everyday word.
